what_it_does: Finding the median value in a continuously arriving stream of data (for example, sensor readings over time) normally requires sorting or tracking every value, which is too slow for near-real-time applications. STREAM is an approximate method that exploits the fact that real-world data streams tend to be locally similar across both space (nearby sensors) and time (recent readings). It groups incoming values into buckets using a clustering technique (similar to the popular K-means algorithm, which automatically groups similar numbers together) and reuses those buckets when the data has not changed much, instead of recomputing from scratch. A tunable knob lets the user trade off how accurate the median estimate is against how quickly it is computed, making it adaptable to different application needs. The abstract suggests clear speed benefits, but specific speedup numbers and the accuracy cost would need to be confirmed in the full paper.
